ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Calculate the operating frequency of the oscillator circuit shown in the figure, if \(C_1 = 0.003\,\mu F\), \(C_2 = 0.003\,\mu F\), and \(L_1 = 50\,mH\). The operating frequency is ______ kHz.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram there is a transistor amplifier stage, and on the right side a resonant network is connected out from near the collector; this network contains inductor L1, as well as two capacitors C1 and C2 split below, with the midpoint grounded. This is a typical Colpitts oscillator resonant tank structure. Reasoning calculation: Calculate according to the resonant frequency of the Colpitts oscillator, the equivalent capacitance of the two split capacitors is the series equivalent value: C_eq = C1*C2/(C1+C2). Given C1 = C2 = 0.003 μF, so C_eq = (0.003*0.003)/(0.003+0.003) μF = 0.0015 μF = 1.5e-9 F. Inductor L1 = 50 mH = 0.05 H. Resonant frequency f = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L1*C_eq)) = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(0.05*1.5e-9)) ≈ 18377 Hz = 18.38 kHz.

Substitute C_eq and L1 into f = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L1*C_eq)), then convert hertz to kHz to obtain about 18.38 kHz.
